title: Community and Infrastructure Services Committee - March 09, 2026

items.title: Commencement
notes: The Community and Infrastructure Services Committee held a meeting this date commencing at 6:32 p.m.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
Consent Items
notes: Pursuant to Chapter 25 (Procedure) of the Municipal Code, a motion was brought forward by Councillor D. Chapman to discuss Consent item 3.1 listed on the agenda, which was voted on and was Carried.

items.title: Uniform Traffic and Parking By-law Updates, DSD-2026-099
notes:
The Committee considered Development Services Department report DSD-2026-099, dated February 18, 2026, recommending that the School Bus Loading Zone previously established on Prospect Avenue be removed; and, that a School Bus Loading Zone be installed on the east (odd-numbered) side of Emerald Avenue from a point 11m south of Prospect Avenue to a point 63m south thereof; and, that parking be prohibited on the north (even-numbered) side of St. Leger Street from Blucher Boulevard to a point 48m east thereof; and, that stopping (8:00am - 4:30pm Monday to Friday) be prohibited on the south (even-numbered) side of Patricia Avenue from Spadina Road West to a point 121 metres west thereof; and further, that the Uniform Traffic Bylaw be amended accordingly.

Councillor D. Chapman noted, the Parents Council for J.F. Carmichael Public School and residents in the subject area have raised concerns regarding the proposed restrictions related to stopping on Patricia Avenue as outlined in the Staff report. In response to questions from the Committee, B. Cronkite noted the proposed restriction on Patricia Avenue addresses congestion on the street resulting from cars stopped or parked for student pick up and drop off. B. Cronkite noted Staff are amenable to having discussions with the neighbourhood residents, the Waterloo Region District School Board and the Parent Council to agree upon an appropriate area for student pick up and drop off within a reasonable distance of the school. In response to further questions from the Committee regarding deferral of this matter to a later meeting date, B. Cronkite requested the Committee approve all the Uniform Traffic and Parking By-law Updates outlined in the Staff report save and except the recommendation related to stopping on Patricia Avenue.

It was requested that the recommendation related to stopping on Patricia Avenue be voted on separately.

Councillor D. Chapman brought forward a motion to approve the recommendation outlined in Development Services Department report, DSD-2026-099 save and except the recommendation related to stopping on Patricia Avenue which was then voted on and was Carried.

Councillor D. Chapman brought forward a motion to defer the recommendation related to stopping on Patricia Avenue to the June 29, 2026 Council meeting, to allow an opportunity for Staff to engage with neighbourhood residents, the Waterloo Region District School Board and the Parent Council of the J.F. Carmichael Public School regarding the proposed changes. The motion was then voted and was Carried.

items.title: Municipal Newcomer Strategy, CSD-2026-030
notes:
At the request of Staff, the Committee agreed to consider this item first rather than the order of items set out in the agenda.

The Committee considered Corporate Services Department report CSD-2026-030, dated February 27, 2026, recommending that Council approved the City of Kitchener's first-ever Municipal Newcomer strategy as attached to report CSD-2026-030 (Appendix A); and that, as an immediate action from that strategy, Council approved annual funding for Immigration Partnership Waterloo Region in the amount of $25,000, to be funded through the City's General Expenses budget; and that all other financial implications of the Municipal Newcomer Strategy be referred to future budget processes.

O. Mise provided a presentation on this matter and responded to questions from the Committee. E. Moorlang was also in attendance and responded to questions from the Committee. R. Morris was also in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee. 

T. Bedard and E. Osei, Waterloo Region Immigration Partnership and K. Al Hariri provided presentations on this matter and responded to questions from the Committee.

Councillor A. Owodunni left the meeting at this time.

items.title: Summary Water Report - 2025, INS-2026-041
notes:
The Committee considered Infrastructure Services Department report INS-2026-041, dated February 17, 2026, recommending that the 2025 City of Kitchener Summary Drinking Water Report be received for information as required by O.Reg. 170/03 Schedule 22 of the Safe Drinking Water Act; and, further that the City of Kitchener provide a copy of the Summary Drinking Water Report to the Township of Woolwich and the City of Waterloo as required by Schedule 22 of O.Reg. 170/03.

A. Mick provided a presentation on this matter. D. McGoldrick was also in attendance and responded to questions from the Committee noting that any potential water supply issues will be assessed through a risk assessment review which will be presented to the Committee at a future meeting. G. St. Louis was also in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee.

items.title: City-Wide Active Transportation Route 2, DSD-2026-029
notes:
The Committee considered Development Services Department report DSD-2026-029, dated February 27, 2026, recommending that staff proceed with wayfinding of Route 2: Stanley Park - Downtown Kitchener - Uptown Waterloo; and, that Pedestrian Crossovers (PXO) Level 2, Type D be installed at the trails outlined in the Staff report and that Neighbourhood Bikeways (shared-use) be installed on streets outlined in the report; and, that the Uniform Traffic Bylaw attached to the report be amended accordingly.

L. Christensen provided a presentation on this matter and responded to questions from the Committee. B. Cronkite and D. Becks were also in attendance and responded to questions from the Committee. 

Councillor P. Singh left the meeting at this time and re-entered.
